Almost every small business owner I know has AI on their phone. Almost none of them have it working inside their business.

The Census Bureau put a number on it: about 37% of companies with 250+ employees are using AI. Businesses with four people or fewer? Less than one in five.

Same tools. Same apps. It's not an access problem — it's a capacity problem.

Three questions to know if you're ready:
→ When someone reaches out, does anything answer before you do?
→ Does your follow-up happen without somebody having to remember it?
→ Could you step away for two weeks and still keep booking?

If any answer is no, that's fixable.

Two minutes, twelve questions: signaturebrandmarketing.com/assessment

#smallbusiness #AI #automation #entrepreneur #smallbusinessowner

We're all competing for a sliver. A sliver of attention.

Ads work — they buy you a bigger piece of it. But once you've got your sliver, what are you doing with it?

If it lands on a page that doesn't answer, a DM that waits till morning, or a phone that rings out to voicemail, you didn't lose because your content was bad. You lost because nothing was built to catch it. And if you paid for that attention, you didn't just lose time — you lost money.

AI is pumping out content at lightning speed. The businesses that win will be the ones with the right systems on the other side.
